summary.title: Put the ZIP code first.
summary.one_liner: Put the US ZIP code at the start of address forms so it can autofill city, state, and country via a free lookup API.
keywords: autofill city and state from zip
takeaways: A US ZIP code alone can determine city, state, and country, so those fields can be autofilled from one input.
Collecting the ZIP first lets street address autocomplete search a much smaller set of addresses.
A free lookup API such as zippopotam.us can fill city and state with a few lines of JavaScript.
Use inputmode="numeric" and proper autocomplete attributes (postal-code, address-line1, country) to help users on mobile and with browser autofill.
Postal codes are not globally unique, so the author suggests country first (pre-filled via IP) for international forms.
summary.summary: This opinionated essay argues that address forms should ask for the ZIP code first, so that city, state, and country can be autofilled from it, with the street address entered last. It criticizes common form anti-patterns such as ZIP fields at the bottom, unsearchable country dropdowns, and forms that lose data on back navigation. The page includes a short JavaScript example calling the zippopotam.us API and offers small HTML tips: inputmode="numeric" and standard autocomplete attributes. It also notes that postal codes are not globally unique, so country-first may be preferable for international use.
